recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future work on broader computable Consent actions should proceed through new or already-open Consent action/modeling issues rather than this DSTU2 future-use request.
issue_request: FHIR-10700 was a Published DSTU2 Consent change request noting that privacy Consent use cases should not be limited to sharing and should also recognize collection, use, and disclosure. The final resolution was Considered for Future Use with a 14-0-1 vote, saying additional use cases would be considered after STU3.
initial_application: No FHIR-10700-keyed source commit or current source reference was found. Later Consent history did broaden the relevant text: commit 24a94d5102 changed the Consent introduction to describe privacy consent as an agreement, restriction, or prohibition to collect, access, use, or disclose/share information; R4B source reconstruction retained matching StructureDefinition language around authorization to collect, use, or disclose information.
additional_context: Consent is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. The current narrative explicitly covers collect/access/use/disclose/share and says only the privacy use case is fully modeled while other scopes may evolve. The current StructureDefinition defines Consent around permitting or denying actions and exposes provision.action with meaningWhenMissing=all actions, while preserving a later caution that the only understood/tested action is read. Community searches found no directly relevant or conflicting Zulip or Confluence records.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. Adding more prose would duplicate current source language or exceed the Jira's future-use disposition.
